text:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: PAGING P1 - AcmeCorp (VPC Private) egress/ingress failures to Redwood NLBs. Incident created INC-2026-0452. Root observed at 2026-03-15T13:12:03Z. Paging oncall.

Mira Patel: ack, I'm here. Seeing customer 5xxs to model endpoints, started ~13:12 UTC. Tagging networking.

Dan O'Leary: I'm on the pager. What's the initial customer impact?

Julia (AcmeCorp SRE): Hi team — from our side ~13:12 we saw a spike of 502/503 on calls to inference.acme.internal. Everything internal to our VPC looks fine, but requests to the Redwood NLB timeout. Sample curl from a customer app:

```
curl -v https://inference.acme.internal/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
* Connected to inference.acme.internal (10.0.12.45) port 443 (#0)
* Failed to receive HTTP response
* Connection timed out after 30001 milliseconds
```

Julia (AcmeCorp SRE): We also tried hitting the NLB private IP directly — same issue. No recent changes on our side except a TF apply earlier this morning related to IAM.

Dan O'Leary: running quick checks on the NLB and target groups.

```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:targetgroup/acme-rtg/abcd1234
{
  "TargetHealthDescriptions": [
    { "Target": {"Id": "10.0.12.45"}, "TargetHealth": {"State": "unhealthy", "Reason": "Target.ResponseCodeMismatch"} }
  ]
}
```

Dan O'Leary: Target count 0 healthy. Health check failures show connection timed out. Checking security groups and VPC route tables next.

Networking change detected: CloudTrail log snippet shows a ModifySecurityGroupRules API at 2026-03-15T13:10:58Z from AcmeCorp's infra role.

Sanjay Rao: I'll take lead. Hypothesis: Egress/security group change removed Redwood's egress path or allowed CIDR to NLB. Proposing short mitigation: re-add outbound SG rule to allow 443 to Redwood-managed egress IPs OR temporarily create a NAT gateway to maintain outbound connections while we investigate. Need @Julia approval for modifying SG in their account.

Julia (AcmeCorp SRE): OK to proceed with the minimal SG change to restore connectivity. Prefer allowlist of Redwood egress IPs rather than a full 0.0.0.0/0. We have an approver on call: julia-approver@acme.example.

Sanjay Rao: copying approved. Executing minimal SG update now: adding outbound rule TCP 443 to 54.88.192.0/24 (Redwood egress) and re-registering targets.

```
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0acme --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 54.88.192.0/24 --description "temp allow Redwood egress - INC-2026-0452"
aws elbv2 register-targets --target-group-arn arn:... --targets Id=10.0.12.45
```

Incident Bot: Action logged: SG update (sg-0acme) by Sanjay Rao at 2026-03-15T13:24:10Z.

Dan O'Leary: re-checking target health after SG change... health checks now returning 200 for most targets.

Incident Bot: NLB target health recovered | healthy count from 0 -> 8 at 2026-03-15T13:28:03Z. Triggering follow-up checks.

Mira Patel: Metrics show request success rate improving to 95% but a small tail (~5%) still getting DNS NXDOMAIN or stale IPs. Looks like some pods/clients cached the old private DNS resolution that no longer points at the internal NLB.

Dan O'Leary: running dig against Route53 private hosted zone used by Acme:

```
dig +short inference.acme.internal @10.0.0.2
# returns nothing for a subset of resolvers
dig +short inference.acme.internal @10.0.1.2
10.0.12.45
```

Dan O'Leary: root cause follow-up: a recent terraform apply (Acme's infra) removed a Route53 record in one AZ's private zone replica during drift correction. The NLBs are healthy but some resolvers still get NXDOMAIN.

Sanjay Rao: mitigation plan for DNS: 1) Recreate missing Route53 record with low TTL to force refresh. 2) Flush local caches if possible (scale restarts for affected pods). 3) Provide Acme with confirmation and request TF fix to avoid drift. I can implement (1) with Acme's consent.

Julia (AcmeCorp SRE): Please proceed. We will coordinate a TF reconciliation tomorrow morning. Thx for the quick SG rollback approach.

Dan O'Leary: applying Route53 record back and setting TTL=30s:

```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123456 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"inference.acme.internal.","Type":"A","TTL":30,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"10.0.12.45"}]}}]}'
```

Incident Bot: Route53 upsert applied at 2026-03-15T13:39:02Z.

Mira Patel: after upsert + SG change success rate to 99.7%. Monitoring for error spikes. No active customer tickets besides initial page.

Ops Lead: Current status update for handoff: mitigations applied (temporary SG egress rule + Route53 upsert). NLB target health restored. Customer impact: degraded for ~16 minutes, now mostly recovered. Blocking items: TF drift in Acme account; need joint postmortem and IaC guardrails (policy to prevent inadvertent SG/Route53 deletes). Plan: coordinate a 0900 PST call with Acme infra, include Redwood infra eng and security.

Sanjay Rao: I'll own overnight monitoring and follow-up ticket INC-2026-0452-FIX to track permanent fixes (IaC guardrails, documented allowlist procedure, confirm NAT fallback options).

Julia (AcmeCorp SRE): Thank you. We'll hold on further TF changes until the call. Please share the action items and the minimal SG change we applied.

Mira Patel: I'll draft the incident summary + RCA and attach logs, CloudTrail snippet, and exact CLI commands used. Will include recommended mitigations: 1) TF guard against accidental SG/r53 deletions, 2) pre-approved egress allowlist procedure, 3) optional Redwood-managed egress proxy for private deployments.

Incident Bot: Status update: INC-2026-0452 -> MITIGATED at 2026-03-15T14:12:03Z. Postmortem placeholder INC-2026-0452-POST created.

Ops Lead: Handoff to night oncall (Sanjay) in 45m. Next steps: monitor metrics, confirm postmortem sent to Acme, schedule sync at 09:00 PST tomorrow. If anything regresses, page with prefix P1 and tag @Ops Lead.

Sanjay Rao: ack. Monitoring dashboards and will keep paged rotations updated.

Mira Patel: closing thread for now, will update postmortem doc when ready. :white_check_mark:
